title: CerviDBF-Net: Leveraging Spatial and Temporal Features for Accurate Cervical Cancer Diagnosis
authors: Sathupati Lydia; Nagadasari Merrin Prasanna
venue: International Journal of Innovative Technology and Interdisciplinary Sciences
abstract: Cervical cancer screening increasingly relies on automated image analysis to support colposcopic assessment and improve the consistency of clinical decision-making. This study proposes CerviDBF-Net, a novel deep learning framework for automated cervix-type classification from colposcopic images. The proposed architecture combines DenseNet121 for spatial feature extraction, a brain-inspired Liquid Neural Network (LNN) for contextual and temporal feature modelling, and a fully connected Softmax layer for final classification. To improve image quality and feature representation, the preprocessing pipeline incorporates bicubic interpolation, Bi-Histogram Equalization with Plateau Limit (BHEPL) for contrast enhancement, Kapur entropy-based thresholding, and the Roberts Cross operator for edge detection. The framework is evaluated on the Intel & MobileODT Cervical Cancer Screening dataset, which contains three cervix types (Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3) defined by the location and visibility of the transformation zone. CerviDBF-Net achieves an accuracy of 98.92%, sensitivity of 99.13%, specificity of 98.38%, precision of 98.69%, and an F1-score of 98.27%, demonstrating strong classification performance compared with the evaluated existing models. The proposed approach provides an automated baseline tool for cervix-type classification that may support triage in colposcopy-assisted screening by helping clinicians assess whether adequate visualization of the squamocolumnar junction has been achieved.

title: THE REFERENCE-RELATIVE REALIZATION PRINCIPLE (RRRP): A General Reference-Relative Systems Principle with a Paradoxical Regime
authors: Shamiul Hoque Shan
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The Reference-Relative Realization Principle (RRRP) proposes a general systems framework inin which the realization of a state, function, signal, representation, process, or output is defined relativeto an explicit reference structure rather than as an absolute property of the system alone. The theoryoriginates from the primary case study The Paradox of Contextualism, in which a subjectively specifiedintention may be evaluated by a generalized system through a reference structure that does not coincidewith the source-intended structure. The resulting apparent contradiction is not treated as a universalimpossibility theorem: exact realization can occur when the relevant equivalence relation is preserved,whereas non-equivalence between source and target reference structures makes exact preservation non-guaranteed. The framework therefore separates default mechanism, generalized principle, and paradoxicalor divergent regimes. A unified architecture represents source formation, encoding, labeling, signaling,projection, processing, medium transformation, target reconstruction, reference-relative evaluation,residual formation, iterative adaptation, and network-level interaction. The model is independent ofany particular criterion or medium: security, accuracy, utility, stability, semantic fidelity, energy, timing,language, code, physical channels, mathematical notation, computational systems, quantum systems,biological systems, and other admissible cases enter as parameterized instances. A finite operationalregime is complemented by an asymptotic regime for iterative realization. Thirty extension case studiesare organized across three analytical layers: Philosophical-Epistemological, Systemic-Mechanistic, andFormal-Mathematical Operational. The manuscript explicitly distinguishes mathematical definitionfrom empirical claim, identifies boundary conditions and counterexamples, and provides a falsifiabilityand anti-pseudomathematics protocol. The result is a general relational principle rather than a claim ofa universal physical law.

title: 音义同源论:语音与语义的编码同源关系|Sound-Meaning Homology: The Encoding Homology of Speech Sound and Semantics
authors: Tonghua (同华) Liu (刘)
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: 摘要 在现代语言学理论中,索绪尔提出语言符号具有任意性,即语音与语义的联结主要依靠社会约定。该理论建立于印欧拼音语言研究基础之上,难以完整解释上古汉字造字阶段的音义生成机制。本文并非否定语言符号的约定属性,而是针对将任意性绝对化的倾向,提出“音义同源论”,考察上古汉字造字阶段音义编码的理据性机制。 本文指出,在上古汉字的造字阶段,语音与语义的结合绝非随机,而是基于特定物理声场与生存场景的强绑定编码。本文结合认知科学的“语音象征”与“意象图式”理论,论证了先民在跨模态感知中,将场景声音(音源原型)与场景意义(义境、义根)进行了同构映射,系统提出了物理映射、生理同构、音场统摄三大实现机制。 传统文献由于“以形索义”,导致音源与义根的解释发生系统性失真。本文完全依托《汉字音源考古》体系的反向工程(由传世文字、古音材料向后倒推上古造字源头的推演路径:音族→字族→义根→音场→义境→音源原型),通过已完成的40余个核心音族及天干、方位等专题实证库,系统重构了汉字音义系统。本文基于字族材料推演提出假说:音可作为义的感知编码,上古阶段存在声义同源绑定机制。通过严苛的内部三重验证与外部证据链,本理论有效杜绝了“俗词源学”的附会,不仅是汉字上古字源考据的核心工作预设,更是探索人类原初认知机制的理论框架。 关键词:音义同源;语音象征;意象图式;反向工程;音源原型;字族铁律 Abstract In modern linguistic theory, Saussure proposed the arbitrariness of the linguistic sign, meaning that the connection between speech sound and semantics primarily relies on social convention. This theory, based on Indo-European alphabetic languages, cannot fully explain the sound-meaning generative mechanism during the creation of ancient Chinese characters. Against the absolute interpretation of Saussure's arbitrariness principle, this paper proposes the theory of "Sound-Meaning Homology" to investigate the perceptual motivation mechanism of sound-meaning encoding in the ancient Chinese character formation stage. This paper argues that during the creation of ancient Chinese characters, the binding of speech sound and semantics was a strong-bound encoding based on specific physical acoustic fields and survival scenes. By integrating the cognitive linguistic theories of "sound symbolism" and "image schema," this paper demonstrates that ancestors performed isomorphic mappings between scene sounds and scene meanings through cross-modal perception, and systematically proposes three implementation mechanisms: physical mapping, physiological isomorphism, and sound field unification. Traditional literature often systematically distorts the explanation of sound sources and semantic roots due to "seeking meaning from form." Relying entirely on the "reverse engineering" of the "Chinese Character Sound-Source Archaeology" system (sound family → character family → semantic root → sound field → semantic realm → sound-source prototype), this paper systematically reconstructs the Chinese character sound-meaning system based on a massive empirical database of over 40 core sound families, the ten heavenly stems, and the four cardinal directions. This paper hypothesizes that sound serves as the perceptual encoding of meaning during the early Chinese character formation. Through strict internal triple verification and external evidence chains, this theory effectively prevents "folk etymology" speculation. It is not only a core working premise for the etymological research of ancient Chinese characters, but also a theoretical framework for exploring the primitive cognitive mechanism of human beings. Keywords: Sound-meaning homology; Sound symbolism; Image schema; Reverse engineering; Sound-source prototype; Character family iron law

title: Modeling Paralinguistic Features for Speech Neuroprostheses: A Systematic Review
authors: Manu Siddharth Yenikapati; Soham Deshpande; S. Desai; Donovan D Santine; Aryan Kia Roghani
abstract: Recent advances in brain-computer interface (BCI) technology have brought speech neuroprostheses closer to restoring naturalistic communication for individuals with severe motor or speech impairments. Although current systems can decode phonemic and lexical information from cortical activity, they often fail to capture paralinguistic dimensions such as intonation, prosody, loudness, and affect that are essential for conveying emotion and intent. This review synthesizes emerging research on modeling and incorporating paralinguistic features into speech neuroprosthetic design. Foundational studies have mapped the cortical organization of speech production, identifying articulatory somatotopy within the sensorimotor cortex and functional subdivisions across planning, phonological, and semantic representations. More recent work has characterized expressive encoding within the ventral precentral and supplementary motor areas, while peripheral and multimodal sensing approaches have demonstrated promising accuracy in decoding emotional states. Collectively, these findings signal a shift toward closed-loop neuroprosthetic systems that integrate affective modulation with linguistic decoding, enabling restoration of speech that is not only intelligible but expressively human. Keywords: Speech neuroprosthesis, paralinguistics, BCI, naturalistic communication

title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration
authors: Neel Dey; Adrian V. Dalca
abstract: Raw image intensities are a poor surrogate for similarity across images in correspondence problems. Further, while auxiliary segmentation labels can provide semantic identification and improve matching, they can assign only coarse identities to fine-grained anatomy and often cover only a subset of structures, particularly in whole-body settings. We present an approach that instead establishes correspondence using complementary representations of anatomy and demonstrate its utility for longitudinal whole-body PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge. We use our 3D foundation model, anatomix, to derive fine-grained, per-voxel semantic representations that are consistent across volumes and further employ off-the-shelf segmentation models to obtain coarse anatomical identities. Together, these representations drive a GPU-accelerated iterative registration solver (FireANTs) in a hybrid multistage framework: the first stage estimates alignment from dense multi-channel features, after which a second refines the deformation using both anatomix- and segmentation-based losses. Lastly, because registration should not introduce non-biological tumor volume changes across time, we develop lesion-specific, component-wise volume preservation schemes. Without any task-specific training, our system placed first on the PSMAReg Challenge leaderboard. Code and interactive visualizations are available at https://www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg.
arxiv_comment: Technical report. First place winning solution for the MICCAI Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg challenge. Code and volumetric visualizations are available at www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg . Keywords: representation learning, medical image registration

title: Nudge the Judge: Uncovering Program Decision Hijacking in Real-World Jev Applications
authors: Yang Luo; Tiantian Ji; Zifeng Kang; Yucheng Wang; Yong Liu; Zhiyi Yin; Xinran Liu
abstract: System One models such as Jev change how software makes decisions by mapping open-ended semantic contexts into structured judgments that directly drive program execution. However, this paradigm introduces a new security risk, which we term Jev Program Decision Hijacking (JPDH): attacker-controlled contexts can redirect program decisions through schema-valid Jev judgments. Existing evaluations focus primarily on model-level attacks or predefined injection channels, leaving attack reachability and downstream security consequences in real-world Jev applications underexplored. In this paper, we present JevProbe, the first automated framework to evaluate JPDH by tracing adversarial influence from reachable context surfaces through program-consumed decisions to downstream security consequences in real-world Jev applications. Our key insight is that application logic maps diverse Jev judgments to observable decisions, enabling systematic, program-grounded attack evaluation. Across 228 popular real-world Jev applications and 2,273 test cases, 81.5% exhibit decision flips, of which 98.6% lead to potential downstream security impacts. Compared with the strongest adapted baseline, JevProbe improves macro-average Decision Flip Rate (DFR) by 50.4 percentage points, while existing defenses offer limited protection. We further construct JevProbeBench to support systematic evaluation of JPDH in real-world Jev applications. We have responsibly disclosed our findings to Jev application maintainers, pending their responses. The source code of JevProbe and the JevProbeBench dataset are publicly available on GitHub (https://github.com/xiaoxiaohg8d/JevProbe-).

title: GeoNIRS: Geometry-Aware Pretraining for Heterogeneous fNIRS Representation Learning
authors: Zongsheng Li; Shengyuan Zhu; Zimo Zhang; Hanyao Li; Shengming Wang; Quanying Liu
abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) provides portable and spatially localized measurements of cortical hemodynamics, but differences in channel count, probe layout, signal distribution, and task type hinder joint pretraining across datasets. We introduce GeoNIRS, a geometry-aware framework that uses source-detector locations as a shared spatial reference across heterogeneous probe layouts. GeoNIRS compresses variable-size channel sets into a fixed-size latent representation and employs bidirectional HbO/HbR cross-reconstruction with contiguous temporal masking. GeoNIRS-base is pretrained on eight heterogeneous datasets, while GeoNIRS-large scales to 22 datasets. Neither downstream data nor labels are used during pretraining, enabling evaluation under a strict cross-task setting. To our knowledge, GeoNIRS is the first fNIRS framework to explicitly model physical channel geometry during joint pretraining across heterogeneous channel configurations, and the first to provide complete source code and downloadable pretrained checkpoints. We evaluate GeoNIRS on eight held-out tasks spanning clinical and auditory assessment, pain and affective processing, semantic decoding, and motor function. GeoNIRS achieves the highest task-averaged balanced accuracy among the evaluated conventional machine-learning, fNIRS-specific, general time-series, and fNIRS pretraining baselines. Compared with random initialization, pretraining improves average balanced accuracy by 4.12 percentage points under linear probing and 3.30 points under full fine-tuning, with larger benefits when labels are scarce. GeoNIRS also remains robust to missing input channels. Geometry perturbations and pretraining ablations further show that both channel geometry and cross-chromophore reconstruction contribute to the learned representations.
arxiv_comment: 30 pages, 5 figures, and 21 tables. Code and pretrained checkpoints are available at https://github.com/GeoNIRS/GeoNIRS

title: LLM-based Code Auditing by Inferring and Evaluating Developer Assumptions
authors: Junming Liu; Marcel Böhme
abstract: When we see a null pointer check, we know that the developer believes that the pointer may not be initialized. If the same pointer is later used without a null pointer check, we may consider this a violation of the developer's belief and ultimately a bug. We develop such a belief-guided program analysis for vulnerability detection (VD). For example, when an authentication function returns the same error for both, a wrong user name and a wrong password, an auditor may infer that the developer believes that both cases are indistinguishable, mitigating a user enumeration attack. This belief is reasonable, as it follows standard security practice. Yet, a function call inducing a difference in response time for both cases, contradicts this belief. This contradiction uncovers a timing side-channel that syntactic analysis tools would miss. Existing static analysis tools struggle with this type of flaw because they require them to be expressible by general, syntactic patterns. Our belief-guided approach detects such domain-specific, high-level semantic security flaws that remain elusive. Given a function, our approach, Creed, infers the developer's security-related beliefs, evaluates how reasonable each one is, and derives the conditions under which it is violated. In contrast to existing ML-based VD techniques, Creed explains the root cause, the symptoms, and the conditions under which each issue is exploitable. To address the context-dependency problem in the evaluation, we introduce two measures for explanation-based VD: recall quantifies how effectively an approach correctly explains a known vulnerability, and overhead quantifies the effort of inspecting its reports. On a recent real-world vulnerability benchmark, Creed detects both semantic and syntactic vulnerabilities more effectively than existing explanation-based VD tools, achieving the best effectiveness-effort trade-off.

title: Harnessing SPAD Noise: Test-Time Gated Attention for Indoor Depth Estimation
authors: Yiquan Gao
abstract: Monocular depth estimation (MDE) has emerged as a cost-effective alternative to hardware-dependent 3D sensing modalities, yet predicting precise metric depth remains a persistent challenge due to intrinsic scale ambiguity, edge bleeding, and limited zero-shot generalization in unseen environments. Recent multi-modal approaches incorporate 1D/3D Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) data to resolve these ambiguities, but they mainly treat SPAD noise as a harmful artifact required for denoising or leave the noise ignored. In this paper, we present an essentially different insight: native SPAD noise is an informative prior that implicitly encodes deterministic environmental characteristics. Driven by this paradigm shift, we introduce a novel, lightweight Test-Time Gated Attention framework by Harnessing SPAD Noise, therefore dubbed HSN. Tailored for indoor scenarios, HSN leverages the synergistic combination of 1D SPAD histograms and Gate Adapters (GAs). Through three complementary optimization phases, it generates channel-wise gated attention vectors to dynamically adjust encoder feature maps at inference time, effectively resolving ambiguous scale and boundary challenges without the heavy computational overhead or dense 3D modalities that other TTA methods suffer from. Extensive experiments on challenging real-world indoor benchmarks show that HSN achieves state-of-the-art metric depth accuracy in in-domain settings, while exhibiting even greater potential under zero-shot generalization to unfamiliar environments. Furthermore, interpretability analysis reveals that the proposed gated attention mechanism adaptively shifts attention toward deeper semantic layers under intensifying SPAD noise. Code will be made publicly available.

title: MiDashengLM-Spatial: Unifying General Audio Understanding and Spatial Awareness
authors: Jinbo Hu; Hang Su; Lichun Fan; Heinrich Dinkel; Gang Li; Zhanchen Dai; Yiru Zhang; Chang Liu; Peng Wang; Junnan Wu; Jian Luan; Cong Zou; Heng Qu
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have achieved strong performance in general audio understanding, yet most are designed for monaural input and discard the inter-channel cues essential for spatial perception. In contrast, existing spatial audio-language models are purpose-built for spatial tasks and fail to capitalize on the general understanding capabilities of monaural LALMs. We present MiDashengLM-Spatial, the first open-source end-to-end unified audio-language model, to our knowledge, which supports both general audio understanding and spatial awareness within a single architecture. It extends MiDashengLM with a spatial audio encoder, Spatial-Dasheng, integrated through a hierarchical semantic-to-spatial conditioning module that injects intermediate semantic representations into the spatial branch at multiple depths while preserving the original semantic pathway. To provide spatial audio-language supervision at scale, we develop a data synthesis pipeline that renders diverse spatial acoustic scenes with scene-level spatial descriptions and question-answer pairs. Experiments show that Spatial-Dasheng achieves strong performance on sound event localization and detection in real-world scenes, and that MiDashengLM-Spatial substantially outperforms existing LALMs on spatial understanding and reasoning benchmarks. Meanwhile, it remains competitive with state-of-the-art 8B-scale LALMs on diverse monaural benchmarks, demonstrating that spatial awareness can be acquired without compromising general audio understanding. The source code and model checkpoint are available at https://github.com/xiaomi-research/midashenglm-spatial and https://huggingface.co/mispeech/midashenglm-spatial.

title: TwinViT-DeepJSCC: Adversarially Robust Semantic Image Communication
authors: Maedeh Fallahreyhani; Paeiz Azmi; Nader Mokari; M. Reza Abedi; Melike Erol-Kantarci; Eduard A. Jorswieck
abstract: Learning-based semantic communication is vulnerable to adversarial perturbations introduced before semantic encoding or over wireless channels. This paper proposes TwinViT-DeepJSCC, a preventive-corrective semantic image transceiver operating under a fixed channel-use budget. Two Vision Transformer (ViT)-based deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) branches learn complementary latent representations protected by sensitivity-aware masking. At the receiver, confidence-aware fusion, blind corruption-severity estimation, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)-severity-conditioned denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM) purification mitigate residual corruption without requiring attack metadata. Experiments on the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research 100-class (CIFAR-100) dataset consider fast gradient sign method (FGSM), projected gradient descent (PGD), natural evolution strategies (NES), and Carlini-Wagner (CW) source-domain attacks, as well as random jamming and channel-aware adversarial waveforms over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and block-flat Rayleigh fading. Under matched channel-use and attack budgets, TwinViT-DeepJSCC achieves maximum peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) gains of approximately 9.5 dB under 20-step PGD and 10.8 dB under channel-aware waveform attacks over block-flat Rayleigh fading. Under PGD, it also improves Top-1 accuracy by up to approximately 38 percentage points over the undefended baseline and 13 percentage points over the strongest competing defense. Ablation results confirm the complementary contributions of the proposed transmitter- and receiver-side mechanisms.
arxiv_comment: 13 pages, 7 figures

title: Visual-Invariance-Augmented Feature Optimal Alignment for Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Closed-Source MLLMs
authors: Xiaojun Jia; Simeng Qin; Yiming Li; Jie Liao; Sensen Gao; Ke Ma; Yang Liu; Xiaochun Cao
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remain vulnerable to transferable adversarial examples, especially in black-box settings where only open-source surrogate models are accessible. Existing targeted transfer attacks mainly align adversarial and target samples using global image-level features, such as encoder [CLS] embeddings. However, such coarse alignment insufficiently exploits patch-level visual structures, limiting transferability across heterogeneous closed-source MLLMs. We propose IAU-FOA, a visual-invariance-augmented feature optimal alignment attack with adaptive unbalanced transport, to improve targeted transferability against closed-source MLLMs. IAU-FOA aligns adversarial and target samples at both global and local levels: a cosine-based objective narrows their global semantic gap, while patch tokens are clustered into compact local patterns and matched through optimal transport for fine-grained feature alignment. Balanced optimal transport enforces fixed marginal masses even for local clusters without reliable counterparts, potentially introducing misleading alignment gradients. We therefore introduce confidence-adaptive unbalanced transport to relax these constraints for weakly matched clusters, aiming to reduce unreliable local alignment and improve adversarial transferability. We further study the effect of input transformations and propose visual-invariance augmentation, which applies bidirectional pixel-intensity rescaling and per-channel white-balance adjustment to simulate exposure, contrast, illumination, and color-temperature variations. This strategy encourages adversarial perturbations to generalize across different visual encoders. Extensive experiments on open-source and closed-source MLLMs show that IAU-FOA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art transferable attack methods. Code is available at https://github.com/jiaxiaojunQAQ/IAU-FOA.

title: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset
authors: Mohammad Abolnejadian; Matthew Brehmer
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset 📄 Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3830398.3830522💻 Code: https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast Supplemental dataset for the paper: InsightToast: Proactive Information Retrieval & Glanceable Visualization in the Side Channel of Data-Rich Meetings Mohammad Abolnejadian and Matthew Brehmer. Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '26). DOI: 10.1145/3830398.3830522 This dataset provides a collection of 43,878 open legislative records from the Canadian House of Commons, spanning 1994 to 2025, covering document types such as debates (Hansard), legislative bills, committee reports, petitions, recorded votes, order papers, and Library of Parliament research publications. It is released at three stages of the same pipeline: the raw collected documents, a processed corpus that has been passed through an ETL pipeline and chunked for use in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, and an embedded, pre-indexed vector store built from that processed corpus. The dataset supports the development and user study of the InsightToast project. The embedded form can be placed directly into the project's codebase, open sourced at https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast, where it serves as the knowledge base when InsightToast operates as a proactive side-channel assistant in policy discussion meetings. Usage in the InsightToast Backend Only qdrant_storage.tar.gz is required to run the backend. Extract it into the root of the InsightToast project, so that qdrant_storage/ sits alongside docker-compose.yml, and start the services: tar -xzf qdrant_storage.tar.gz -C /path/to/InsightToast/ cd /path/to/InsightToast docker compose up --build -d Contents File What it is Approx. size parliament_data.tar.gz Raw source corpus of 43,878 parliamentary records, as 57,124 files (.txt + .pdf) 8.1 GB compressed / 11 GB extracted parliament_data_processed.tar.gz Processed corpus: the same records cleaned, normalized, and chunked into RAG-ready JSON 2.1 GB compressed / 9.1 GB extracted qdrant_storage.tar.gz Pre-indexed Qdrant vector store, ready to mount as the knowledge base 21 GB compressed / 27 GB extracted parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the raw corpus, viewable without downloading the archive small parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the processed corpus small qdrant_storage.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the vector store small SHA256SUMS.txt SHA-256 checksums for the three archives small Verify the archives after download: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt Source Corpus: Raw Parliamentary Documents parliament_data.tar.gz contains open legislative documents collected across the range of record types produced by the Canadian House of Commons and the Library of Parliament, including the proceedings of debate, the texts of bills as tabled, the reports of standing committees, the petitions presented to the House, and the recorded outcomes of divisions. The documents were assembled from three public sources: the House of Commons (ourcommons.ca, including the Legislative Information service, LEGISinfo), the Library of Parliament of Canada (parl-gc.primo.exlibrisgroup.com), and the independent open-data mirror openparliament.ca. No private, personal, or access-restricted material is included; Member of Parliament profiles contain only information published in an official public capacity. Total: 43,878 parliamentary records, distributed across 57,124 files (43,634 .txt + 13,490 .pdf). Each record is provided as extracted plain text, with the source PDF alongside it under the same basename where one exists, so records that carry both formats account for two files. Temporal coverage: documents span the 35th through 45th Parliaments. Debates run from 1994-01-17 to 2025-10-10; coverage of the other record types varies by type. Languages: the source records are bilingual (English and French), as published by Parliament. Filename conventions: debates use sitting dates (YYYY-MM-DD- .txt); bills, journals, order papers, and votes use - - (for example, 37-1-C-10); petitions and Library of Parliament publications use slugified titles. Category Files Description debates/ 18,347 House of Commons debates (Hansard transcripts), one file per sitting day bills/ 10,561 Legislative bills, full text plus the original tabled PDF journals/ 7,038 Official Journals of the House (daily record of decisions) petitions/ 6,093 e-Petitions and paper petitions presented to the House votes/ 4,521 Recorded division and vote results order-papers/ 4,228 Order Paper and Notice Paper (daily agenda) library/ 2,202 Library of Parliament publications and tabled agreements committee-reports/ 1,577 Standing and joint committee reports, grouped into 27 committee subfolders politicians/ 1,319 Member of Parliament profiles research/ 1,210 Library of Parliament research and HillNotes publications committees/ 28 Committee mandate and description summaries Total 57,124 See parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt for the full breakdown, including all committee subfolders. Processed Corpus: Cleaned and Chunked Records parliament_data_processed.tar.gz contains the same corpus after the ETL pipeline that turns each document into retrievable units. Documents are parsed from their metadata header and routed by document_type. Bilingual records are language-identified with langdetect and reduced to their English content by an LLM pass. PDFs are structurally partitioned with unstructured's partition_pdf into text, table, and image elements; table elements are linearized into prose by an LLM, and salient figures are captioned, written to images/, and linked from their chunk via has_images. Records whose content is inherently tabular, namely recorded votes, petitions, and Member profiles, are rendered into natural-language narratives to keep them semantically retrievable rather than reducing to fields. Type-specific pre-segmentation then splits debates on speaker turns, preserving the speaker, section, and timestamp, before every stream passes through a RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (1,000 characters, 200 overlap); each resulting chunk is tagged with its content_type (text, table, or image) and its provenance. The output is one JSON document per record, holding the record's metadata and its ordered list of chunks: { "metadata": { "document_type": "debate", "session": "35-1", "date": "1994-01-17", "language": "en", "source_file": "debates/1994-01-17-1.txt", "source_url": "...", "total_chunks": 51 }, "chunks": [ { "chunk_id": 0, "content": "...", "metadata": { "speaker": "...", "section": "...", "content_type": "text", "has_images": false } } ] } Volume: 42,014 JSON records and 2,170 extracted images, totaling 6,379,732 chunks, which is the set embedded into the knowledge base below. Traceability: every record's metadata.source_file links back to its file in the raw corpus. Coverage: most record types are processed in full; committee-report and library are present as subsets of the raw corpus. See parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt for per-category counts. Indexed Knowledge Base qdrant_storage.tar.gz contains the processed corpus above embedded and indexed into Qdrant, ready to serve as the retrieval backend with no further processing. title: A new image similarity metric for a perceptual and transparent geometric and chromatic assessment
authors: Antonio Di Marino; Vincenzo Bevilacqua; Emanuel Di Nardo; Angelo Ciaramella; Ivanoe De Falco; Giovanna Sannino
abstract: Full-reference image quality assessment metrics such as PSNR and SSIM misalign with human perceptual judgments on texture and shape distortions, a limitation documented across multiple benchmarks. Deep perceptual metrics such as LPIPS substantially close this gap but produce opaque scores that cannot be attributed to specific image regions, a concern amplified by emerging Artificial Intelligence regulation requirements. We propose EDOKS (Earth mover’s Distance and Oklab Similarity), a white-box full-reference IQA metric that decomposes perceptual dissimilarity into two interpretable terms: a texture term, computed via Earth Mover’s Distance on Gabor filter signatures, and a chromatic term, computed as pixel-wise Euclidean distance in the Oklab perceptual color space. Evaluated on the Berkeley-Adobe Perceptual Patch Similarity dataset, which includes traditional, CNN-generated, and geometric distortions, EDOKS outperforms all tested low-level full-reference competitors on both the JND and 2AFC subsets, measured respectively by correlation with human judgments and agreement with human choices, achieving results close to deep perceptual metrics without any learned parameters. Beyond the scalar score, EDOKS produces pixel-level heatmaps that localize texture and chromatic discrepancies independently, exposing failure modes invisible to luminance-based metrics and providing users with verifiable evidence for the assigned similarity score.
